alloc::clone_binary_heap.note: Opt-in recursive heap cloning and explicit destruction execute on Linux x86_64 through the GPU compiler and preserve Min/Max order. All five focused groups pass, covering independent nested owners, priority multiplicities, empty/zero-sized values, 13 typed allocation failures, 16 owned-error paths and all 96 reached owned-error allocations. Ordinary inherent collection methods retain their documented shallow policy.

alloc::clone_deque.note: Opt-in recursive deque cloning and explicit destruction execute on Linux x86_64 through the production GPU compiler. All four focused groups pass, with 379 logical ring cases, 13 reached nested allocation failures, six owned-error paths and 33 owned-error allocation failures. Ordinary inherent Deque methods retain their documented shallow policy; the guide defines actual-owner and borrowed-alias cleanup.

alloc::clone_hash_map.note: Opt-in recursive hash-map cloning and explicit key/value destruction execute on Linux x86_64 through the GPU compiler. All four focused groups pass, covering independent nested owners, collisions/tombstones, typed rollback, 14 reached allocation failures, 18 owned key/value errors and changed key identity. Ordinary inherent collection methods retain their documented shallow policy.

alloc::clone_hash_set.note: Opt-in deep HashSet cloning and explicit destruction execute on Linux x86_64 through the GPU compiler. Three focused groups pass, including 557 sequence/failure/identity cases, six owned errors, all 39 reached allocation failures, independent String owners, empty and zero-sized keys. Ordinary inherent set methods retain their shallow policy.

alloc::clone_tree_map.note: Opt-in recursive ordered-map cloning and explicit key/value destruction execute on Linux x86_64 through the production GPU compiler. All five focused groups pass, covering independent nested owners, sorted staging, transfer/reset, empty/zero-sized values, 15 reached clone-allocation failures, 12 owned key/value errors and three changed-key cases. Ordinary inherent TreeMap methods retain their documented shallow policy; unrelated generic replay dependencies remain separate.

alloc::clone_tree_set.note: Opt-in deep TreeSet cloning and explicit destruction execute on Linux x86_64 through the GPU compiler. Five focused groups pass, including independent String owners, a 512-state ordered model, observable O(n log n) construction, nine reached allocation failures, typed owned errors and changed-key checks. Ordinary inherent set methods retain their shallow policy.

core::clone_values.note: Opt-in scalar and structural cloning executes on Linux x86_64 through the GPU compiler. Five native groups pass: fourteen exact scalar types with true empty Infallible errors, active-only Option/Result cloning, Pair rollback, nested String/Vec owners, minimal bounds, eighteen callback cases, fourteen owned errors, all 45 reached allocation failures and four source rejections. Scalar Destroy does nothing because scalars own no resource; wrapper Destroy releases only active owners. No implicit moves, Drop or pointer/view owner implementations.

ext::archive_index.note: Persistent immutable ZIP snapshots and ordinal catalogs execute through SQLite on Linux x86_64/glibc. Seven focused native groups cover binary duplicate names and keys, all-entry CRC preflight, independent owners, pinned read consistency, explicit transaction uncertainty, native faults and 29 import plus 23 read allocation failures. The real archive-index program imports, lists, reads and exports a measured 1,024-entry, 8 MiB expanded archive.

ext::openssl_digest.note: Digests execute through OpenSSL 3 EVP on Linux x86_64/glibc with checked native C linking and an explicit libcrypto dependency. The raw extern declarations require caller-managed native pointer and lifetime contracts.

ext::openssl_tls.note: Client and server TLS execute through OpenSSL 3 libssl/libcrypto on Linux x86_64/glibc. The server's six native groups pass 53 cases for credentials, noninteractive encrypted keys, binary transfers, closure/truncation, retry stability and native/allocation cleanup. Mandatory client trust/identity rejection also passes after adding explicit session roles. Manual contexts/sessions borrow connected nonblocking sockets; callers provide deadlines and SIGPIPE policy. Server client authentication is explicitly Unauthenticated; mTLS, callbacks and broader security APIs remain separate work.

ext::sqlite.note: SQLite database and prepared-statement owners execute on Linux x86_64/glibc through checked C linking with an explicit sqlite3 dependency. Native gates cover 558 typed-value cases, 640 model commands, real persistence and locks, 21 native failure modes and four staging allocation failures. The linked guides define strict value access, ownership, limits, cleanup and the measured bulk workload.

ext::tls_stream.note: Shared buffered client/server TLS streams execute on Linux x86_64 through OpenSSL 3. HTTPS GET passes 62 cases across four groups after the context ownership change; the bounded HTTPS health/echo service passes 106 cases across four groups. Server construction consumes its socket on every result and retains a native context reference; streams own only their optional client context. Deadlines, byte/call budgets and manual cleanup are explicit. TLS and sensitive operations remain in OpenSSL; mutual TLS, automatic resolution, redirects, keepalive and concurrent scheduling remain separate work.

std::command_raw.note: Internal syscall support for std::command. Use the checked command API and its ownership contract for ordinary programs; this inventory does not make the raw helpers a separate support promise.

std::gpu.note: User buffer/dispatch extern declarations have no runtime binding. Compiler use of a GPU does not establish user GPU execution.

std::host.note: Descriptor/status helpers describe an unavailable host service; this module supplies no host operation.

std::net.note: The direct legacy network service declarations are unbound. Metadata helpers describe that unavailable service; executable owned sockets use std::socket over std::linux separately.

std::thread.note: Thread spawn/join/yield/current-ID extern declarations have no runtime binding. Source metadata helpers do not implement threads.

std::time.note: Counted monotonic/system clock reads, unix_seconds and i32 sleep use native bindings. The three i64-return/read or i64-sleep extern declarations noted below remain unbound; their presence does not establish executable clock support.

declarations.monotonic_now_ns: Unbound legacy i64 host declaration. Use the checked std::clock/std::time_checked API and its linked target contract.
declarations.system_now_unix_ms: Unbound legacy i64 host declaration. Use the checked std::clock/std::time_checked API and its linked target contract.
declarations.sleep_ms: Unbound legacy i64 host declaration. Use the checked std::clock/std::time_checked API and its linked target contract.

std::vec.note: Protected extraction identity and a remaining binary-heap backing dependency. Legacy failure/owner policies differ from alloc::vec; ordinary programs use alloc::vec. This source inventory creates no compatibility alias or new support promise.

test::harness.note: Descriptor/status metadata supplies no registration, discovery or runner. Explicit source testing is implemented separately by test::suite, test::check, test::property and test::bench.
